extracted.intended_audience: Makueni County officials, community organizers, civil society groups and citizens participating in or organising county-level public participation
extracted.subtask_description: A county-level formal guideline describing the legal basis, goals, models, forum types, composition rules, meeting frequencies, and expected impacts for organising public participation across village-to-county levels in Makueni County, Kenya.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and constitutional basis for public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation is a constitutional requirement: Article 1 (sovereign power belongs to the people), Article 10 (2) (a), Fourth Schedule Part 2 (14) of the Constitution of Kenya, and Sections 87 to 92 and 115 of the County Governments Act, 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public participation is stipulated as a function of the County Government and must be facilitated in accordance with these constitutional and statutory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and core principle of public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation is a structured way of consulting with persons, groups and entities before decisions are made; it is designed to give a voice to the voiceless and cements the concept of agency to the County Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is not meant to convey decisions already made; it should generate and confirm decisions. It is a non-partisan process in which the agent goes to 'take instruction and direction' from the people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government commitment to people-centered and people-driven development
rubrics_metrics.description: The County government will promote and ensure people-centered and people-driven development as anticipated by the constitution and will continuously strive to create an enabling environment for citizen involvement from the initial stages of policy development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure citizens are involved early in development of policies, not only at later stages; the enabling environment includes accessible forums and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models/levels of participation to be utilized
rubrics_metrics.description: The government will seek to utilize the various levels of participation: consultation, placation, partnership and citizen control models of participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select among these models as appropriate to the matter at hand; the framework commits to promoting all these models to achieve meaningful engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of participation — Informing
rubrics_metrics.description: Informing: the public by providing information to help them understand the issues, options and solutions;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, accessible information dissemination so the public can understand context and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of participation — Consulting
rubrics_metrics.description: Consulting: with the public to obtain their feedback on alternatives or decisions;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design mechanisms (surveys, meetings, submissions) that solicit and record feedback on proposed alternatives or decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of participation — Involving
rubrics_metrics.description: Involving: the public to ensure their concerns are considered throughout the decision making process particularly in the development of decision criteria and options;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure participants' concerns are tracked and demonstrably influence criteria and option development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of participation — Collaborating
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborating: with the public to develop decision criteria and alternatives and identify the preferred solutions;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use collaborative processes (joint workshops, co-design sessions) where public participants help craft options and select preferred solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of participation — Empowering
rubrics_metrics.description: Empowering: the public by placing final decision making authority in their hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where empowerment is used, public bodies must delegate final decision authority to the citizens or their representatives as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntariness of participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in all forums and development committees is purely voluntary and no benefit whatsoever shall accrue to members because of their engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation cannot be mandatory nor used as basis for benefits; ensure recruitment and membership respect voluntariness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Village Peoples Forum — composition and operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Village Peoples Forum: each village (approx. 3,455 villages) will invite all people from the village but at least 100 people (one from each household) per village forum; each forum elects/selects an 11-person committee to form the Village Development Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Village forums shall hold meetings quarterly; the elected 11-member committee represents the village at higher cluster forums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Village Clusters Peoples Forum — composition and operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Village Clusters Peoples Forum: at least 315 clusters (each ≈13 villages) with ~143 participants (11 representatives from each of the 13 villages); each cluster elects/selects an 11-member Cluster Development Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cluster forums meet quarterly; persons from the cluster beyond village committees can attend; government representatives at this level are ex-official members; the Administrator and a community member shall co-convene and co-moderate the forum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-Ward Peoples Forum — composition and operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sub-Ward Peoples Forum: 60 fora covering 3–5 village clusters each, with 53–75 people; membership includes 11 representatives from each of the 3–5 village clusters and 20 co-opted representatives of organized groups; each Sub-Ward elects an 11-member Sub Ward Development Committee plus ~15–25 co-opted representatives to represent it at the Ward Forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-Ward forums meet bi-annually; County/National government reps and community representatives convene/moderate; the County Government and a community representative form the Secretariat; regional balancing shall be considered when selecting representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ward Peoples Forum — composition and operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ward Peoples Forum: approximately 30 fora with 72–92 members drawn from two Sub-Wards (11 members from each sub ward, 15–25 co-opted members from village clusters, 20 organized group representatives); each Ward elects an 11-member Ward Development Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ward forums meet bi-annually; the County government representative (Ward Administrator) and a community representative manage the secretariat; respective elected leaders attend as ex-officials; organized groups nominate persons to attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-County Peoples Forum — composition and operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sub-County Peoples Forum: one in each of the six Sub-Counties with 53–97 people, comprising 11 from each ward and 20 representatives of organized groups; each sub-county elects 11 persons from Ward Development Committees and 20 nominated by Sub County Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-County forums meet bi-annually and represent an intermediate deliberative level feeding into the County forum.

rubrics_metrics.name: County Peoples Forum — composition and operation
rubrics_metrics.description: County Peoples Forum: one county forum with around 1,000 people including 11 from each of the 60 Sub-Wards, 10 representatives of each organized group, 140 county government officials, and 660 members of Sub Ward Development Committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The County Forum convenes once annually; it is co-chaired by the County Budget and Economic Forum (CBEF) and a community representative; the Governor and Deputy Governor shall also co-chair; the County Secretary and a community representative run the secretariat; organized groups are nominated per sub ward as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election/selection of 11-member development committees at each level
rubrics_metrics.description: Each forum (village, cluster, sub-ward, ward, sub-county) shall elect/select an 11-person committee to form the relevant Development Committee (e.g., Village Development Committee, Cluster Development Committee) that represents the forum at the next level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These committees shall meet at least according to the prescribed frequencies (e.g., quarterly for village/cluster, bi-annually for sub-ward/ward/sub-county) and serve as representative bodies for upward representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forum governance roles: conveners, moderators and secretariat
rubrics_metrics.description: At cluster level the Administrator and a community member shall co-convene and co-moderate the forum; at Sub-Ward the County Government and a community representative form the Secretariat; at County level the County Secretary and a community representative run the secretariat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government officials often attend as ex-official members; community representatives should co-manage convening and moderation to ensure shared ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation from organized groups — nomination and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations to forums shall be done from organized groups including KNUT, KUPPET, KESSHA, KEPSHA, MYWO, National Youth Council, CBOs, KNCCI (County Chapter), hawkers representatives, faith-based organizations (list given), farmers groups, boda boda groups, Most Affected Persons (MAPs), Professionals in the Diaspora, People with Special Needs (PWSN), Children representative, PTAs, town committees, PMC representatives, minority and marginalized groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All the groups to be represented where applicable; numbers of nominated representatives from organized groups vary by forum level (e.g., 20 at sub-ward, 10 per organized group per sub ward for County forum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional balancing and co-option rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When electing or co-opting representatives (e.g., ~15–25 co-opted representatives to Sub-Ward forums, 15 members co-opted to wards), regional balancing will be considered in obtaining representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection processes should consciously aim for balanced geographic/regional representation within the forum's area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting frequency by forum level
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribed meeting frequencies: Village and Cluster forums — quarterly; Sub-Ward, Ward and Sub-County forums — bi-annually; County Peoples Forum — once annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the scheduled frequencies for convening to ensure timely input at each stage of planning and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected social impact of public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Public participation helps in alleviating social conflicts by bringing different stakeholders and interest groups together and helps minimize both the number and magnitude of social conflict arising over the course of implementation of policies, laws and development plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design participation to foster stakeholder dialogue and conflict mitigation; monitor social conflict indicators to assess impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected economic impact of public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: An enlightened citizen will effectively participate in the development process hence influence decision making which will impact on their livelihoods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether participation leads to decisions that improve livelihoods; use economic indicators and feedback to evaluate effectiveness.
